messages:
josh: Escalation from Alice (customer). Streaming endpoint intermittently returns partial chunks then connection drops after ~25-40s. Happens across regions. Started ~after last runtime deploy. Raising here for quick triage. :rotating_light:

alice: Repro steps I gave:
1) curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' "https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams/resp?model=xlarge" \n2) client sends comment ping every 15s (just a single line ":ping\n\n")
Observed behavior: first ~3 chunks stream fine, then either we get a partial token line and connection resets, or the stream stalls and client reconnects. No HTTP 5xx from API, connection just closes.

alice: Quick logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T14:02:13Z] stream open id=abc123 200
[2026-03-16T14:02:28Z] send chunk id=abc123 seq=3 len=48
[2026-03-16T14:02:41Z] keepalive comment from client :ping
[2026-03-16T14:02:42Z] upstream write error EPIPE
[2026-03-16T14:02:42Z] connection closed id=abc123
```

sam: Pinging eng-runtime. Can you share connection traces / proxy logs? EPIPE suggests remote closed socket. Could be proxy idle timeout or upstream backpressure causing closure.

maria: Also check ALB/NLB idle_timeout and any intermediate CDN/edge. Some proxies drop connections that are ":comment" lines (they treat as no-data) if they expect activity.

alex: Quick question — are these comment pings exactly ":ping\n\n" (SSE comment) or are they sending a full event like `event: keepalive\ndata: ok\n\n`? Some load balancers treat packets with just a colon as TCP keepalive and may not reset idle timers. Others ignore them.

alice: They are literally SSE comments (single-line starting with ":"). We added them because customer said token gaps cause client-side timeouts unless we send something.

josh: Repro command from customer (minimal):
```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=xlarge' | stdbuf -oL awk '{print; fflush()}'
```
Client side sends periodic comment via separate connection hook, not on the same TCP stream.

sam: Two immediate checks: 1) confirm ALB idle_timeout (default 60s) and proxy upstream write limits, 2) enable conn-level keepalive (TCP) on both sides. If client uses separate connection for pings, that won't keep upstream stream alive.

maria: There's a known case where our edge (edge-proxy v2.14) aggregates empty comment frames and then forwards nothing for a while under heavy backpressure — could cause perceived stall then downstream close. I added an alert to look for aggregated small writes.

alex: Can we get a pcap or a curl --trace-ascii capture? Also need the request id from customer's logs (they included id=abc123 above).

alice: I've attached trace snippet: `--trace-ascii trace.log` shows client side still had socket open until we saw RST from server side.

josh: Short-term mitigation suggestions to give customer:
- Switch SSE keepalive to send a tiny comment as part of the same streaming TCP connection (server-side send ":heartbeat\n\n" every 10s) rather than spinning up another socket.
- Enable client reconnect with Last-Event-ID and exponential backoff.
- Increase ALB idle_timeout to 120s (if using ALB).

sam: Runtime action items:
- eng-runtime to add a debug flag that forces a heartbeat event (not comment) for repro testing.
- eng-infra to check edge-proxy v2.14 behavior under small-write aggregation.

josh: Example server-side keepalive we recommended to the customer:
```
# send a raw SSE comment line on the same connection every 10s
:heartbeat\n\n
# or send a simple ping event which some proxies treat as data
event: ping
data: ""
```

maria: Note: some proxies treat `:comment` as lower priority and may drop it under backpressure. `event: ping` tends to be forwarded as data. Worth testing quickly.

alex: Also adding a small change to runtime: when we detect consecutive small writes (<100B) to same client socket we will insert a real ping event every 15s for a debug rollout. Assigning to @sam for a canary.

sam: Will run a canary in us-west-2 with instrumented debug logs. I will post the correlation id and tcpdump shortly.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: eng-runtime/heartbeat-canary v0.3 -> canary-us-west-2

sam: Canary deployed. Captured tcpdump shows server sending `event: ping` bytes periodically on the same TCP stream; no EPIPE observed in canary runs so far.

josh: I'll respond to customer with mitigation steps and ETA for a runtime canary. Asking Alice to try switching to `event: ping` if they can, or to let us run in canary.

alice: Thanks — will test `event: ping` and report back within the hour. :pray:

josh: Closing loop: assign eng-runtime and eng-infra to investigate edge aggregation write path. Escalation priority: P2.

alex: Added issue #INF-893 in our tracker with logs and initial traces.

josh: Thanks all.
